This is actually a huge issue in taxonomy. It is often referred to as the "species problem". Basically scientists to this day can't agree on exactly how to define species largely because it's humans trying to put nature/life in a box. Nature/life does not fit into neat little boxes. We like putting things into boxes because it makes shit easy for us, so we try.

This is problem is especially relevant when people try to state whether all "humans" are the same race/species or not. We don't have a clear definition of species, so stating with any confidence either way is just showing your lack of knowledge in the field of biology. Some people think a Pug and a Great Dane are both Canis familiaris. Some don't.

So it's just a matter of how high you set the bar for genetic differences between populations. Set it low enough and Europeans who interbred with Neanderthals and Africans who interbred with an unknown hominin would be considered different species.
